## Rule

Input 2×6: row0 = all color A, row1 = all color B. Output = column-parity row-swap
(checkerboard interleave): **`Output[i][j] = Input[(i+j)%2][j]`** → row0 `[A,B,A,B,A,B]`,
row1 `[B,A,B,A,B,A]`. NOT identity/transpose/flip/rotate of the whole grid.

**LIVE bar = cost 30** (manifest, owner Vamshi; `ng_current_bar.py --task 373`), sha
`efaa28a5…3ba3c`. NOTE: the auto STATUS/GRAPH-DIAG blocks below are STALE (old 642/1067
Slice/Gather/Pad graph); the live best is a single Einsum `ncab,a,h,w,ndhe->nchw` with a
shared `sign[30]` = `[1,-1,1,-1,1,-1,0×24]`, memory 0 / params 30.

## Algorithm sketch

`out[n,c,h,w] = sign[h]·sign[w]·(Σ_{a,b} in[n,c,a,b]·sign[a])·(Σ_{d,e} in[n,d,h,e])` — a
rank-1 outer product `P[c]⊗sign[h]⊗sign[w]`, argmaxed per channel to recover colors. The
period-2 `sign` (column/row parity) is the only stored payload.

## Cost analysis

Cost model = `memory + params`; live best = single Einsum, 0 intermediates → **params 30**
(the length-30 `sign` parity vector). **Floor = 30 (WALL, 2026-07-07).** Forced-component
argument: the output alternates period-2 along columns, but the input carries no
column-varying signal (each row is one constant color), so the parity MUST be injected
externally. The only memory-0 route is a single output-producing node (any intermediate is
charged in bytes; the smallest useful full-canvas op ≫30B). A single node emitting the
checkerboard needs a length-30 parity payload (Einsum operand indexed by a length-30 canvas
axis is forced =30 — empirically ONNX rejects length-6). Procedural generation swaps those
30 params for a ≥30B intermediate + scalars (no better). Hence cost ≥ 30; the live Einsum
sits on the floor. cost≤1 perfect-25 route does NOT exist for this task.
